page0.text:
I walk up the stone steps.
Saber is already armed.

page1.text:
...
...
Both of us are tense, expecting an enemy to attack at any moment.
The stairway up to the mountain gate is long, and the breeze is pleasantly warm despite us being in the hills.

page2.text:
According to Saber, this mountain has a barrier that repels Servants.
If they attempt to approach Ryudou Temple by any other path besides the gate, the barrier hurts them and reduces their magical energy.
Therefore, the only way into Ryudou Temple is up these stairs.

page3.text:
"I was sure they'd try to ambush us. You don't sense any Servants, Saber?"
"No.
I am the only Servant on these steps—"
Suddenly, Saber halts and looks down.

page4.text:
"Saber...? What happened?"
"...It must have been my imagination. I thought I saw something that resembles a katana, but there's nothing like that here.
The gate is unprotected. Let us go inside."

page5.text:
Saber ascends the stone steps quickly.
"Hm?"
After a moment's confusion, I run after her.

page6.text:
Inside, it's silent.
The wind is strong.
The shadows, deep.
It's terribly dark, even though the moon is out.

page7.text:
...
I look up.
The moon's out, all right.
It glows brightly, illuminating the unlit temple grounds.
Despite that, the area is engulfed in shadow.

page8.text:
"Saber."
"Yes, something is wrong. The lack of response to our entry is inconcievable. And it's too quiet."
"...Let's look around inside. A family of almost fifty runs Ryudou Temple.
There's no way it would be this quiet."

page9.text:
I enter the temple with Saber.
There's nobody around.
After making sure the grounds are unoccupied, Saber and I head deeper into the buildings.

page10.text:
Everybody inside is asleep.
They show no signs of waking.
They don't react even when I touch or pick them up.
Every single one of the fifty or so monks is in a coma.
All of them lie in a pleasant, dreamlike sleep, breathing steadily.

page11.text:
Of course, one of my classmates is among them.
Issei Ryudou is asleep. I've only seen him so relaxed on a handful of occasions in the privacy of the student council office.

page12.text:
...
We move quickly through the wood-floored hallways.
Saber senses something.
She directs us towards the inner main shrine.
The Master behind this disaster must be lurking in the heart of the temple.

page13.text:
We step into the main shrine.
Suddenly, my eyes are greeted by scarlet blood all over the floor.

page14.text:
"...!?"
The center of the shrine is drenched in red.
There's a man on the floor.
There's a pool of red spreading out from him. Maybe he was stabbed through the chest.

page15.text:
The wound is fatal. He's lost too much blood to survive.
He's already dead.
He looks familiar, and he must be the Master of the thing standing besides him.

page16.text:
The Servant stands there, staring down at her Master's lifeless corpse.
"..."
I'm assailed by a headache and an alarming unease.
It isn't the gruesome scene that terrifies me, but—

page17.text:
That thing...
That dagger...is something bad.
Saber doesn't seem to sense it, but somehow, I can tell the power in that dagger is nothing good.

page18.text:
"Caster!"
Saber stands ready to fight.
Caster, the purple-robed Servant, doesn't react.
Is it because we've caught her by surprise, or because she was caught red-handed?
Saber slightly crouches, ready to attack Caster in a breath.

page19.text:
"No, Saber! Wait!"
"Why are you stopping me, Shirou!? This is our chance to defeat Caster—"

page20.text:
"Not that, I mean don't touch that dagger! It destroys magecraft. It might sever the contract between Master and Servant!"
"Then Caster, your Master..."

page21.text:
"..."
We don't know for sure if she killed her Master.
But it's clear to me that the dagger in her hand has an incomparable ability to dispel magical effects.

page22.text:
"Caster, you would slay your own Master!?"
Saber advances angrily.
...Caster turns to look at us.
Her lifeless demeanor makes her look more wraith than Heroic Spirit.

page23.text:
A sword flashes through the air.
Saber's sword splits Caster's robe, shredding her clothes as she evades by bounding backwards.

page24.text:
"Sa...ber...?
You must be here to finish me off. I don't know who put you up to this, but they're thorough."

page25.text:
"Silence. I don't want to hear the words of one who betrays her lord.
"Ha! You think I killed my Master? That I would hurt Souichirou?
Heh...Haha, hahahahahaha! How amusing. Yes, if I had known this would happen, perhaps I would have done it myself!"

page26.text:
She coughs blood as she laughs.
The black-clad mage conceals the strange dagger under her robe, and thrusts a hand at Saber.

page27.text:
"You're an eyesore, Saber. Disappear along with your Master."
...
There's nothing else to say.
Watching Caster keenly, Saber swings her sword without hesitation.

page28.text:
...Caster fades away.
Their clash couldn't even be called a fight.

page29.text:
Caster may have outstanding magecraft, but it was completely ineffective against Saber's high Magic Resistance.
Saber shrugged off Caster's barrage of spells and cut her down in a single blow.

page30.text:
"I've defeated Caster. Your orders, Master."
"Uh. R-right. Well, there's nothing else to do here. I could call the hospital...or actually, I should let Kotomine take care of the rest. He should be able to help all the unconscious people."

page31.text:
...But there's no saving the dead man in front of us.
Caster disappeared, leaving her Master's body behind.
...His death will be buried in darkness.
Tonight, he took his last breath, and one day, he will disappear from people's memories, his final fate unknown.

page32.text:
"Shirou."
"...I know. There are four more Masters. I can't afford to freeze up here."
"That is wise of you to say. I understand how you feel, but please try not to become sentimental."

page33.text:
Saber turns her back on the shrine.
...
I'll at least burn the sight of the fallen corpse into my memory before I follow her.

page35.text:
"Shirou? Why did you stop?"
"Huh? Uh, um, for a second it felt like we were being watched. Didn't you feel it, Saber?"

page36.text:
"I did not sense anything. We have already checked the surroundings for other people. Are you sure you didn't just imagine it?"
"Ugh...maybe. I bet you're right, Saber. Yeah, it was probably nothing."

page37.text: "Then let us hurry. Now that Caster has fallen, her victims will begin to wake up. We should leave before we are sighted."

page38.text:
...She's right.
It leaves a bad taste in my mouth, but this should put an end to the comas happening all over the city.
I can chalk that up as a win, at least.

page39.text:
"All right. Let's leave the mountain and let Kotomine know. Then we'll go home and rest."
Saber nods in satisfaction and leaves the shrine.
